subChunks.title: clsx, tailwind-merge, and CVA
subChunks.hookHtml: Knowing utility classes is the easy part. The hard part is wiring them to component logic — variants, props, overrides — without your JSX becoming an unreadable string of concatenated conditions. Three small libraries solve this completely, and every serious React + Tailwind codebase uses them.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Sable the Illuminator: "These three — clsx, tailwind-merge, class-variance-authority — are the entire authoring layer for Tailwind in React. Master them and your components become readable. Ignore them and you will be maintaining spaghetti string concatenation forever."

Problem 1: Complex conditional classes

String concatenation works but becomes unreadable fast. clsx is the solution:

import { clsx } from 'clsx';

// Conditional expressions
clsx('px-4 py-2', isActive && 'bg-blue-600', isDisabled && 'opacity-50')
// → 'px-4 py-2 bg-blue-600'  (if active, not disabled)

// Object syntax
clsx('px-4 py-2', {
  'bg-blue-600 text-white': isPrimary,
  'opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed': isDisabled,
})

Problem 2: Tailwind class conflicts when merging

If a component sets px-4 and a caller passes className="px-8", both end up on the element. Which wins depends on stylesheet order — unpredictable.

tailwind-merge understands Tailwind's utility groups and resolves conflicts:

import { twMerge } from 'tailwind-merge';

twMerge('px-4 py-2', 'px-8')     // → 'py-2 px-8'
twMerge('text-sm', 'text-lg')    // → 'text-lg'
twMerge('bg-red-500', 'bg-blue-600')  // → 'bg-blue-600'

The cn() pattern — combine both

// lib/utils.ts
import { clsx, type ClassValue } from 'clsx';
import { twMerge } from 'tailwind-merge';

export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
  return twMerge(clsx(inputs));
}

// Usage:
<button
  className={cn(
    'px-4 py-2 bg-blue-600 text-white rounded-md',  // base
    className,           // caller override — conflicts resolved by twMerge
    isDisabled && 'opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed',
  )}
>

class-variance-authority (CVA) — typed component variants

import { cva, type VariantProps } from 'class-variance-authority';

const button = cva(
  'inline-flex items-center justify-center font-medium rounded-md transition-colors duration-150 focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-offset-2 disabled:opacity-50 disabled:pointer-events-none',
  {
    variants: {
      variant: {
        primary:     'bg-blue-600 text-white hover:bg-blue-700 focus-visible:ring-blue-500',
        secondary:   'bg-white text-gray-700 border border-gray-300 hover:bg-gray-50 shadow-sm',
        ghost:       'text-gray-700 hover:bg-gray-100',
        destructive: 'bg-red-600 text-white hover:bg-red-700 focus-visible:ring-red-500',
      },
      size: {
        sm: 'text-xs px-3 py-1.5',
        md: 'text-sm px-4 py-2',
        lg: 'text-base px-6 py-3',
      },
    },
    defaultVariants: { variant: 'primary', size: 'md' },
  }
);

type ButtonProps = VariantProps<typeof button> & React.ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>;

function Button({ variant, size, className, ...props }: ButtonProps) {
  return <button className={cn(button({ variant, size }), className)} {...props} />;
}

// Fully typed, IntelliSense shows all options:
<Button variant="secondary" size="lg">Cancel</Button>

Sable: "This is how Shadcn/ui builds every component. The variant declaration is the component's contract — a typed API."

storyBeats.text: Sable the Illuminator arranges three small crystal vials on the workbench. They look almost trivial — but every master's work you've seen lately has used all three.

storyBeats.speaker: Sable the Illuminator
storyBeats.text: String concatenation works until it doesn't. clsx cleans up conditional logic. tailwind-merge resolves conflicts when classes collide. Compose them into cn() and you never think about either problem again.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a complete button system showing all four variants and two sizes:

  • .btn (base): inline-flex, items-center, gap-2, font-medium, rounded-md, transition-colors, duration-150, text-sm, px-4, py-2
  • .btn-primary: bg-blue-600, hover:bg-blue-700, text-white, shadow-sm
  • .btn-secondary: bg-white, border, border-gray-300, hover:bg-gray-50, text-gray-700, shadow-sm
  • .btn-ghost: hover:bg-gray-100, text-gray-700
  • .btn-destructive: bg-red-600, hover:bg-red-700, text-white
  • .btn-sm: text-xs, px-3, py-1.5
  • .btn-lg: text-base, px-6, py-3
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a reusable Badge component in HTML/CSS from scratch. It should have a base style (small, pill-shaped, semi-transparent) and accept override classes for colour. Demonstrate the twMerge pattern by writing the component twice — once with broken class merging (two conflicting bg classes) and once fixed.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Without tailwind-merge, what bug occurs when a reusable component accepts a className prop and internally sets padding? Show the bug with a concrete example, then show how twMerge fixes it.

questions.explanation: tailwind-merge understands that px-4 and px-8 are in the same utility group. The later value (px-8) wins and px-4 is dropped. The result is py-2 px-8.

questions.prompt: A component applies className={cn('text-sm font-medium', props.className)}. A caller passes className="text-lg font-bold". What is the final resolved class string?
questions.explanation: tailwind-merge (via cn) resolves both text-sm/text-lg and font-medium/font-bold conflicts. The caller's classes win, producing font-bold text-lg.

questions.prompt: What specific advantage does CVA (class-variance-authority) give over nested ternaries for button variants, besides readability?
options: CVA exposes TypeScript types via VariantProps automatically — callers get IntelliSense for valid variant values and TypeScript errors on invalid ones
CVA automatically resolves conflicting Tailwind utility classes at runtime
CVA reduces bundle size by tree-shaking unused variants at build time
CVA generates CSS classes without requiring Tailwind at all
questions.answer: CVA exposes TypeScript types via VariantProps automatically — callers get IntelliSense for valid variant values and TypeScript errors on invalid ones
questions.explanation: Nested ternaries are not typed — TypeScript cannot infer which strings are valid variant values. CVA's VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants> gives the component a proper typed API, catches typos at compile time, and documents the variant contract in one place.
